data.reasoning: The disagreement stems entirely from tool errors, not security findings. deepseek-v4-flash successfully reviewed all 8 files including the PKGBUILD and found no issues: standard binary package downloading from official GitHub releases with pinned SHA256 checksums, simple package() function copying binaries, and a benign .install script that only echoes usage instructions. The other two reports failed due to API errors (qwen3-235b: HTTP 400 on PKGBUILD; openrouter/free: parsing failures on multiple files, but marked advisory:true so doesn't count). The initial PKGBUILD audit for makepkg --printsrcinfo succeeded in all three reports, confirming no dangerous top-level code execution. This is a textbook safe AUR binary package.
data.disagreement_analysis: Tool errors caused the inconclusive verdicts: qwen3-235b encountered HTTP 400 when reviewing PKGBUILD, openrouter/free had parsing failures on .gitignore/LICENSE/PKGBUILD (advisory report). deepseek-v4-flash completed successfully. No model found actual security issues.

openrouter/free: Failed to parse decisions for .gitignore, LICENSE, and PKGBUILD (advisory report, doesn't count toward verdict)
learnings: API errors (HTTP 400, parsing failures) should trigger automatic retry or fallback rather than marking files inconclusive
When one model successfully reviews all files and finds no issues while others fail due to tool errors, the successful review should be weighted more heavily
Advisory reports (advisory:true) should be clearly separated from voting reports in disagreement detection to avoid false disagreement signals
